title: Software Testing
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: Software Testing.

items: Code review — Human examination of source code for flaws
Static Application Security Testing (SAST) — Automated source code analysis
Finds vulnerabilities before deployment (shift-left security)
Can detect: buffer overflows, SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded credentials
Peer review and pair programming complement automated tools

blocks.text: Code review methods range from informal to highly structured:

rows: Rigid formal process with defined entry/exit criteria, roles (moderator, reader, recorder, author), and stages (planning, overview, preparation, inspection, rework, follow-up)
Author walks through code with reviewers; less rigid than Fagan
Developers review each other's code informally
Two developers work together in real-time; continuous review
Tools scan source code/bytecode for known vulnerability patterns

blocks.text: From the ISC2 Study Guide: "Fagan inspections follow a rigid formal process, with defined entry and exit criteria that must be met before transitioning between stages. The Fagan inspection level of formality is normally found only in highly restrictive environments where code flaws may have catastrophic impact." From Chapple: "During a code review, also known as a 'peer review,' developers other than the one who wrote the code review it for defects. Code reviews may result in approval of an application's move into a production environment, or they may send the code back to the original developer with recommendations." ⚠️ Exam Trap: Fagan inspection is the MOST FORMAL code review method. It has six specific stages and defined roles. The exam tests whether you know that Fagan inspections are for high-assurance environments where code flaws could have catastrophic consequences. Most organizations use less rigorous peer review. ⚠️ Exam Trap: Static analysis (SAST) analyzes CODE without executing it. It complements but does NOT replace human code review — automated tools can miss business logic flaws that a human reviewer would catch.

items: Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) — Tests running applications
Black-box testing — No source code access; tests from outside
Finds runtime vulnerabilities that static analysis may miss
Tests actual behavior under various inputs and conditions
Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST) — Combines SAST and DAST

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: SAST analyzes CODE (doesn't need a running application). DAST analyzes a RUNNING APPLICATION (doesn't need source code). They complement each other and should be used together.

items: Sends random, malformed, or unexpected input to an application
Designed to find crashes, memory leaks, and unhandled exceptions
Generational (intelligent) fuzzing — Creates input based on data model understanding
Mutation fuzzing — Modifies known-good inputs randomly
Highly effective at finding zero-day vulnerabilities

blocks.text: From Chapple: "Generational (intelligent) fuzzing develops data models and creates new fuzzed input based on an understanding of the types of data used by the program." Fuzzing is effective because:

items: Developers often don't test edge cases
Automated fuzzers can run millions of test cases
Finds vulnerabilities that manual testing misses
Particularly good at finding buffer overflows and format string vulnerabilities
API testing — Verifies APIs handle input correctly and enforce access controls
UI testing — Validates user interface behavior and security controls
Physical interface testing — Tests hardware interfaces for vulnerabilities
Integration testing — Verifies security across component boundaries
Focus on input validation, authentication, authorization, and error handling
